question: What does one real 1,024-row prompt layer-step cost on the GPU (the routed experts' block tiles + the cold set's upload), against the measured 56-70 ms host layer-step?
bench: c/tests/bench_cuda_moe.cu (make -C c cuda-moe-bench), the code commit after this file's base: PLAN 15.11
box: RTX 5070 12 GB sm_120, i5-10400F, 23 GB RAM, CUDA 13.4; one GPU process at a time
budget_note: 7.18 GiB of resident expert weights = 2,296 experts of 3,072 (the 64K tier's 7.47 GiB = 2,296 from bench/results-whole.json: the same set, the bench's rows padded to words on a synthetic table)
steps_note: 24 layer-steps + the 12 loop layers (6..17) twice more, each layer its own routing and format
gflop_note: 1,024 rows x top-8 x (gate 2*I*D + up 2*I*D + down 2*D*I) at D 2,304, I 1,152 (the snapshot's moe_intermediate_size, not the 768 the plan assumed)

rows.tile_padding_note: the tiles compute ceil(rows/64)*64 rows an expert: 61% padding at 8192 rows over 128 experts of a heavy-tailed history; 137% at 128-row tiles (COLI_CUDA_MOE_TILE128 would be wrong at this shape)

contend_note: a 1 GiB KV-mirror copy issued on a second stream in each step's window (79.1 ms on its own at 12.64 GB/s): the step becomes 89.8 ms, i.e. the mirror copy and the expert stream do not share the bus; at 64K the engine's whole mirror is ~0.6 GiB over 63 chunks, so this is the worst case of landing it all in one step
overlap_note: the prefetch does not hide the upload on this box: the copy itself stays 2.13 ms (layer 6's 28.7 MiB) but the frame's submit grows 8.23 -> 10.37 ms, and at 90.9 MiB a step the sequence is 16.04 -> 15.42 ms. A raw two-stream probe (a 91 MiB copy 7.01 ms, a spin kernel 2.64 ms) overlaps to 7.06 ms, so the limit is the tiles' own latency-bound reads meeting the DMA's writes, not the driver's streams
proj_note: derived: prefill - (host_expert - ms*steps/1000), host 127.0 s over 2,268 steps at 64K and 658.1 s over 8,784 at 250K; attention unchanged. 250K's attention+other floor is 1,021.8 s, so 1,155 s is not capped

question: The same at the 250K tier's residency.
box: RTX 5070 12 GB sm_120, i5-10400F, 23 GB RAM, CUDA 13.4

provenance: derived from the two measured cells
decision: GPU prompt-MoE: the 36-step sequence is 15.4 ms a layer-step at 75% and 21.1 ms at 56%, both far under the gate's 35 ms and against the measured 56-70 ms host step; the projection is 64K prefill 156 s (was 248.0) at 75% and 169 s at 56%, 250K 1,155 s (was 1,678.0) and 1,205 s, uncapped by attention (the floor is 1,021.8 s)
hybrid_note: the tiles alone are 8.2 ms (75%) / 6.8 ms (56%) and the residents carry 98.7% / 94.1% of the routed rows: a hybrid that leaves the non-resident pairs on the host is bounded by max(device, host) = 18.5 s / 15.3 s of expert work at 64K, i.e. ~10 s better than streaming them. It needs a filtered host pair step; the streaming path needs no host change, so it is the one prototyped first
upload_note: at 56% the cold set is 166.7 MiB a step, 369 GiB over a 64K prefill's 2,268 steps (30 s of PCIe), against the host path's measured 18.8 GiB over the same prefill: the streaming path pays PCIe for what the tier's RAM cache already holds
